content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV cache cardinality spike detected in rope-scaling pools (ntk/yaRN sliding-window workloads). Error budget burn > 8% across eu-west-1; auto-throttle engaged.

maria: I’m oncall for this shift, pulling up dashboards. seeing a big increase in kv evictions + continuous-batch lat tail. impact: some Dedicated customers with long-context requests are getting 500s and high p99.

devon: adding context — we started shipping the sliding-window prefetch for longer ctx clients last night (canary). looks like NTK heuristic misfires for sequences > 64k and causes repeated kv prefetch fanout.

sam: logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z rope-ntk-03 kernel: kv_prefetch: window=65536 requests=312 fwd=311 evict=298
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z batcher: continuous_batcher: batch_size=48 latency_ms=3400 p99=11300
2026-03-15T09:12:08Z runtime: kv_miss_ratio=0.87 total_kv_ops=1.2M
```

maria: good signal. how widespread? only canary fleet or across regions?

devon: so far eu-west-1 and us-west-2 show correlated spikes. canary config was pushed as a global startup flag in the rope-host template by mistake — should have been env-scoped.

jin: model side — YaRN longctx workloads do many prefix replays; with sliding-window prefetch enabled we’re duplicating KV fills across NTK shards. memory churn + eviction cascades.

sam: proposed immediate mitigations:
- disable sliding-window prefetch on rope host pool via rollout flag
- reduce continuous-batch max_window from 65536 -> 16384 to reduce batch fanout
- enable KV backpressure (reject prefetch queue when miss_rate > 0.6)

maria: agree. prioritize minimal blast radius. devon, can you flip the flag? include a quick canary before global.

devon: doing a targeted flip to rope-canary hosts now. command I’ll run:
```
# disable sliding-window prefetch for rope canary
rbctl set feature rope.sliding_window_prefetch false --env rope-canary --actor devon
```

opsbot: Deploy job started: deploy/rope-config-toggle (id: d-9981). 6 hosts targeted.

maria: watch metrics: kv_evictions, continuous_batch.latency.p99, request_errors. paging oncall for SRE for escalation.

sam: after flip: initial telemetry shows drop in kv_evictions by ~72% on canary within 60s, p99 down from 11s -> 1.2s. good sign.

jin: we should also hotpatch the NTK heuristic to gate sliding-window on seq_len < 32k and model_type == "yarn_long" until we have proper shard-aware prefetch.

devon: I can push a temporary runtime override too:
```
# runtime override (hotfix)
/ops/hotfixes/rope/runtime_override.yaml
fields:
  ntk.sliding_window_max_seq: 32768
  ntk.prefetch_enabled_for_model_types: ["yarn_short","rope_base"]
```
Applying to dedicated pools in 2 min for controlled rollout.

maria: support: please post a customer advisory for affected Dedicated tenants and flag tickets. set temporary SLO leniency.

sam: I’m adjusting autoscaler thresholds to avoid aggressive spinup which was amplifying KV churn. changed prefetch concurrency limit from 8 -> 3.

opsbot: deploy/rope-config-toggle succeeded on canary. next: promote to 60% of rope-hosts? (yes/no)

devon: promote to 60%. I’ll keep 40% as fallback.

maria: monitoring: all good on canary -> promoting. keep alerts for any p50/p95 regressions.

15m later — sam: global stats after promotion: kv_evictions down 63% cluster-wide, p99 latency down to 1.1s on average. request_errors reduced 85%.

jin: note for follow-up: we need a proper prefetch sharding plan and NTK update to avoid duplicate fills across YaRN shards. add to backlog and assign owners.

maria: customers impacted: 3 Dedicated accounts saw transient failures, support notified, tickets created: #SUP-4221, #SUP-4222, #SUP-4223. no data loss.

devon: postmortem owners: devon (runtime), jin (inference), sam (sre). ETA draft 48h.

maria: closing pages and demoting to monitoring. leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed (severity: P2). Duration: 00:43:10. Autoclosed alerts: kv_eviction_rate, continuous_batching_p99.
